seoTitle: JWT Sign & Verify with RS256, PS256, ES256 in the Browser
metaDescription: Generate RSA or ECDSA key pairs, sign JWTs with a private key and verify them with a public key using WebCrypto. Keys stay in your browser.
intro: Create and check JSON Web Tokens signed with public-key algorithms (RS256/384/512, PS256/384/512, ES256/384/512).
why:
Choose generate, sign or verify. Generating creates a key pair and prints PKCS#8 and SPKI PEM plus the public JWK. Signing takes a JSON payload and a PKCS#8 private key (PEM or JWK) and returns the compact token; ECDSA signatures use the raw r||s form the JWS spec requires. Verifying checks the signature with a public key and shows the payload.

The algorithm is chosen by you, never by the token header (a basic defence against algorithm-confusion attacks); verification checks the signature only, so real code must also check exp, nbf, iss and aud. Output was cross-checked with the jsonwebtoken library in both directions.

The file is read in your browser and is not uploaded anywhere.
howTo: Pick an algorithm and generate a key pair.
Switch to sign, paste the payload and the private key.
Copy the token, or switch to verify and paste a token with the public key.
Never paste production private keys into a page you do not control.

faq.a: ES256 is compact and fast; RS256 is the most widely supported; PS256 is RSA with a modern padding scheme.

faq.q: My key says BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY.
faq.a: That is the older PKCS#1 form. Convert it: openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -nocrypt -in key.pem -out pkcs8.pem.
No. Verify the claims in your application code.
The file is read in your browser and is not uploaded anywhere.
